description: The documentation covers the configuration options for the search index plugin, including precedence rules, default settings, and keys with their effects. It also mentions files the plugin writes and how to exclude noise.

nodes.title: Configuration
nodes.summary: The search index configuration file is auto-generated and has a precedence order of explicit function options, environment variables, `.opencode/ai-context.config.yaml`, and built-in settings. The file is used to define search index settings, with the plugin being opt-in per repository.
nodes.bodyText:
# Configuration

Precedence, highest first: explicit function option (tests only) > env var >
`.opencode/ai-context.config.yaml` (team-shared, committable) > built-in
default ([ADR-0014](adr/0014-project-config-file-precedence.md)). The file is
auto-created on first start with every key and its default value; restart
opencode after editing it. The generated file is the reference for every
setting (default, effect, environment variable); there is no separate example file. The plugin is **opt-in per repository**
([ADR-0029](adr/0029-opt-in-enabled-flag-and-default-template.md)): the
generated file has `enabled: false`, and while it is off (or the key is missing)
the plugin only keeps the file and does nothing else. Set `enabled: true` to
switch it on.

children.title: Keys
children.summary: This documentation covers the configuration options for a search index plugin, including keys, environment variables, default settings, and their effects. Key terms include `enabled`, `data_dir`, `model_cache_dir`, `embed_dims`, `heavy_mode`, `max_memory_mb`, `embed_threads`, `embed_concurrency`, `embed_max_tokens`, `max_file_bytes`, `os_notifications`, `allowed_repos`, `exclude`, `install_skills`, `agent_hint`, `tool_log`, `tool_log_full_responses`, `reranker`, `file_summaries`, `summary_llm`, `reindex_chunks`, `reindex_summaries`, and `shared_worker`.
children.bodyText:
## Keys

| YAML key | Env var | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `AI_CONTEXT_PLUGIN_ENABLED` (`1`/`0`) | `false` | Master switch. Off: no index, no indexing, no worker, no tools, no agent hint, no skills/`.gitignore` writing, no popups; only the config file is provided. A missing key counts as off. |
| `data_dir` | `AI_CONTEXT_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR` | `~/.local/share/opencode-ai-context-plugin` | Per-project SQLite stores. Must be outside the worktree (else the plugin's writes re-trigger indexing). |
| `model_cache_dir` | `AI_CONTEXT_PLUGIN_MODEL_CACHE_DIR` | shared HF cache | Private model cache (air-gapped setups). |
| `embed_dims` | `AI_CONTEXT_PLUGIN_EMBED_DIMS` | unset (768) | Matryoshka truncation, 1..768; faster search, slightly lower quality. Changing it requires a re-index. |
| `heavy_mode` | `AI_CONTEXT_PLUGIN_HEAVY_MODE` | `false` | No functional effect today. |
| `max_memory_mb` | | `6144` | Soft RSS ceiling of the host while indexing; over it the indexer GCs, waits, then stops with a readable error. |
| `embed_threads` | | `6` | onnxruntime threads. Lower = less CPU/fan. |
| `embed_concurrency` | | `3` | Files indexed in parallel and inferences the shared worker runs at once. `1` = sequential. |
| `embed_max_tokens` | | `512` | Hard cap per embedded text; chunks are split to fit. Attention memory grows quadratically. |
| `max_file_bytes` | | `1048576` | Larger files are skipped and listed in the status file; retried when they change. |
| `os_notifications` | `AI_CONTEXT_OS_NOTIFICATIONS=0` | `true` | OS popups for start, finish and failure. |
| `allowed_repos` | | `[]` | Names (no hash) of other indexed projects this repo may search; written by `ai_context_allow_repo`, applied without restart. A legacy `ai-context/config/allowed-repos.json` is imported once. |
| `exclude` | | `[]` | gitignore-style patterns never indexed (on top of `.gitignore`); excluded directories are not descended into. |
| `install_skills` | `AI_CONTEXT_INSTALL_SKILLS=0` | `true` | Install the bundled skills (`index-status`, `cross-repo`) into `.opencode/skills/`. |
| `agent_hint` | | `true` | Append the tool-preference rule block to the system prompt. |
| `tool_log` | | `false` | Write every tool call (time, tool, session, arguments truncated to 200 chars, response summary: size, counts, first paths, error, empty) to `.opencode/ai-context/tool.log.md`. Git-ignored; at 5 MB the file is rotated to `tool.<time>.log.md` and the newest 10 rotated files are kept. |
| `tool_log_full_responses` | | `false` | With `tool_log`: no truncation at all: complete arguments and complete response text. Code of this repo and of linked repos then lands in the log; see [data boundary](data-boundary.md). |
| `reranker` | - | `true` | Cross-encoder re-ranking of search results. |
| `file_summaries` | - | `true` | One summary chunk per multi-chunk file. |
| `summary_llm` | - | oMLX `http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1`, `Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct-MLX-4bit` | Block `base_url`, `model` (exact name), `api_key_env?`, `timeout_ms?`; `false` disables the LLM. The API key is never read from the file (a literal `api_key` is ignored with a warning): export it as `AI_CONTEXT_SUMMARY_LLM_API_KEY` or the variable named by `api_key_env`; without one no key is sent. On HTTP 401 the user gets an OS popup and an `index_status` notice ("API key not set. Set it with: export AI_CONTEXT_SUMMARY_LLM_API_KEY=<your key> and restart opencode"). Failures fall back to deterministic summaries, which are flagged (`detsum` in the stored fingerprint) and rewritten, summary only, on a later start once the LLM answers; Markdown doc-tree summaries are skipped. Also writes the doc-tree node summaries. Requests carry `tool_choice: "none"` (retried without it on HTTP 400) so servers that inject global MCP tools answer with prose; answers that are JSON tool calls are rejected. File content is sent to `base_url`; keep it local ([data boundary](data-boundary.md)). |
| `reindex_chunks` / `reindex_summaries` | - | `false` | One-off, reset to `false` by the plugin after a finished run. `reindex_chunks` re-chunks and re-embeds every file (stored summaries kept), `reindex_summaries` rewrites the file summaries only, both `true` re-index everything. A failed or aborted run keeps the flags on. |
| `shared_worker` | `AI_CONTEXT_SHARED_WORKER=0` | `true` | Run embeddings in one shared background process. |

`AI_CONTEXT_PROJECT_FILES=0` disables writing project files (config, skill,
gitignore); used by the unit tests.

children.title: Files the plugin writes
children.summary: The plugin writes configuration settings, live index progress, versionable backups, bundled skills, and a live index to specified paths.
children.bodyText:
## Files the plugin writes

| Path | Purpose | Commit? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.opencode/ai-context.config.yaml` | settings | yes |
| `.opencode/ai-context/index-status.json` | live progress | no (auto-ignored) |
| `.opencode/ai-context/backup/index-NNNN.jsonl` (+ `doc-trees.jsonl`, `graph.jsonl`) | versionable index backup, shards of about 10 MB | optional |
| `.opencode/skills/index-status/`, `.opencode/skills/cross-repo/` | bundled skills (`managed-by` marker; remove the marker to own one) | optional |
| `.opencode/.gitignore` | ignores the volatile status file; existing lines are kept | yes |
| `<data_dir>/projects/<key>/index.sqlite` (+ doc trees, graph) | live index | no |
| `<data_dir>/embed-worker.sock`, `embed-worker.log` | shared worker | no |

children.title: Excluding noise
children.summary: This configuration excludes files from being indexed, specifically those in the `legacy/` directory and any files with a `.generated.ts` extension. Changes to these files or re-indexing will remove the stored chunks of excluded files.
children.bodyText:
## Excluding noise

```yaml
exclude:
  - legacy/
  - "*.generated.ts"
```

Stored chunks of newly excluded files are removed when the file changes or is
re-indexed.

description: The plugin works locally, indexing and searching on the user's machine. It does not control what happens to data after it is handed to the agent. Tool results and cross-repo search go to the agent's LLM, which sends them to a configured model provider. The plugin cannot detect or restrict code leaving the machine.

nodes.title: Data boundary: what is local, what is not
nodes.summary: The plugin operates locally and does not influence data processing after it is passed to the agent.
nodes.bodyText:
# Data boundary: what is local, what is not

The plugin itself works locally. It does **not** control what happens to the
data after it has been handed to the agent.

children.title: Stays on your machine (the plugin)
children.summary: The plugin indexes and stores files locally, using embeddings and SQLite. It uses a local server for file summaries and sends file content to the `summary_llm` endpoint. The repo-local backup contains chunk text, doc trees, and a symbol graph, which is published when the repository is committed and pushed.
children.bodyText:
## Stays on your machine (the plugin)

- Indexing, chunking, embeddings (ONNX, shared worker), re-ranking, SQLite
  stores and the call/import graph. No code or query is sent anywhere by the
  plugin's index and search path.
- File and document summaries use the `summary_llm` endpoint. The default is
  a local server (`127.0.0.1`). The plugin sends file content there. Its API
  key comes from an environment variable only, never from the committed config.
- The repo-local backup (`.opencode/ai-context/backup/`) is plain text that
  contains chunk text, doc trees and the symbol graph. It lives in the
  repository, so committing and pushing it publishes that content to whatever
  hosts the repo.

children.title: Outside the plugin's control
children.summary: The plugin's control is limited to the agent's LLM, which processes search results and sends them to a configured model provider. It cannot detect or restrict the retrieval of code snippets from cloud services or other indexed projects.
children.bodyText:
## Outside the plugin's control

- **Tool results go to the agent's LLM.** Everything `semantic_search`,
  `search_docs`, `find_symbol`, `analyze_impact`, `repo_structure` and the
  admin tools return (code snippets, document text, summaries, paths, status)
  becomes part of the conversation. opencode (or the ACP client) then sends it
  to the configured model provider. If that provider is a cloud service, the
  retrieved code leaves the machine, under that provider's terms and retention.
  The plugin cannot detect or restrict this.
- **Cross-repo search** (allowlist) makes other indexed projects' content
  retrievable, and therefore sendable, in the same way.
- **`summary_llm`**: pointing `base_url` at a remote endpoint sends file
  content to that endpoint.
- Hints and skills the plugin installs only steer the agent; they are not an
  access control.

children.title: Recommendations
children.summary:
- **Confidential Code**: Use local or contractually acceptable models.
- **Summary LLM**: Keep on a local server.
- **Allowed Repos**: Review before enabling cross-repo search.
- **Tool Log**: Write responses to `tool.log.md`; do not attach unreviewed.
- **Backup Content**: Check before committing to shared/public repos.
- **Exclusion Paths**: Exclude sensitive paths from indexing.
children.bodyText:
## Recommendations

- For confidential code, use a model provider you consider local or
  contractually acceptable, not just a local index.
- Keep `summary_llm` on a local server.
- Review `allowed_repos` in `.opencode/ai-context.config.yaml` before enabling cross-repo search.
- `tool_log_full_responses: true` writes tool responses (repo code) to the git-ignored `tool.log.md`; do not attach that file to bug reports unreviewed.
- Check the backup content before committing it to a shared or public repo.
- Exclude sensitive paths from indexing (`exclude`, see [configuration](configuration.md)).

description: This documentation covers the development workflow, testing procedures, and conventions for a search index. Key terms include npm scripts, mise, ADRs, test units, and code conventions.

nodes.title: Development
nodes.summary: This documentation covers the development process for a search index, including commands for installing dependencies, running type checks, unit tests, building the application, and installing plugins. It also mentions using Mise for a self-contained setup with pinned Node versions.
nodes.bodyText:
# Development

```bash
npm install
npm run typecheck     # tsc --noEmit
npm run test:unit     # node:test via tsx, no build step
npm run build         # esbuild: plugin bundle + worker bundle in dist/
./scripts/install-plugin.sh
npm run dump-ast      # inspect a tree-sitter AST while writing extractors
```

With [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/), `mise.toml` wraps the same commands
(`mise run test`, `mise run typecheck`, `mise run setup`) with a pinned Node
version; `build`, `test`, `typecheck` and `setup` run `npm install` first, so a fresh checkout needs only `mise install && mise run setup`. It is self-contained so the package can be extracted to its own repo.

children.title: Workflow
children.summary: The text covers the workflow for testing and implementing code changes, including writing or updating failing tests, implementing the changes, running type checks and unit tests, and keeping steps small with one hard-to-reverse decision requiring an ADR.
children.bodyText:
## Workflow

Test first: write or update the failing test, implement, then run
`npm run typecheck` and `npm run test:unit`. Keep steps small; one decision
that is hard to reverse gets an ADR in [adr/](adr/README.md).

children.title: Testing
children.summary:
- Unit tests for search index functionality in `test/unit/` using `node:test`.
- Mock stores must implement `listFiles`, `getChunksPage`, `getIndexStatus` for doc-tree stores.
- Tests lock tool naming scheme and essential description content.
- Tests must close timers or sockets to prevent hanging run.
children.bodyText:
## Testing

- All tests are unit tests in `test/unit/` (`node:test`); stores use temporary
  directories, embedders and workers are injected fakes.
- `test:unit` sets `AI_CONTEXT_OS_NOTIFICATIONS=0`, `AI_CONTEXT_INSTALL_SKILLS=0`,
  `AI_CONTEXT_PROJECT_FILES=0` and `AI_CONTEXT_SHARED_WORKER=0` so tests never
  pop up notifications, write project files or spawn a worker.
- Mock stores must provide `listFiles`, `getChunksPage`, `getIndexStatus`
  (and `countTrees`, `listPaths` for doc-tree stores).
- `test/unit/tool-descriptions.test.ts` locks the tool naming scheme and the
  essential description content.
- Tests that open timers or sockets must close them; a leaked handle hangs the
  run (the worker's idle timer once did).

children.title: Conventions
children.summary: - **Conventions** document outlines coding practices and versioning strategies for the search index. It emphasizes IDE integration, dependency management, file chunking and indexing changes, and specifies version bumps for code and embedded text updates. Additionally, it notes macOS script caveats regarding `timeout` and `sed -i` usage.
children.bodyText:
## Conventions

- Prefer the code intelligence of the IDE; no new dependency without need.
- Changing how files are chunked, tree-indexed or summarized? Bump `CODE_INDEX_VERSION` /
  `DOC_INDEX_VERSION` (`src/indexing/indexing.ts`, [ADR-0027](adr/0027-self-healing-reindex.md));
  changing embedded text or vectors bumps `EMBED_FORMAT_VERSION` instead.
- Comments only where the code needs clarification.
- macOS caveats for scripts: no `timeout`, `sed -i` needs a backup suffix.

The plugin does nothing until enabled in a repository, creating necessary files and starting the first index. nodes.title: Installation
nodes.summary: The plugin is a single bundled file and worker script installed globally in opencode's config directory, covering every repository. The installation process involves running `npm install` and `npm run build`, followed by executing the script `./scripts/install-plugin.sh`.
nodes.bodyText:
# Installation

The plugin is one bundled file plus one worker script, installed into
opencode's **global** config directory so one install covers every repo
([ADR-0015](adr/0015-single-bundled-plugin-file.md)).

```bash
npm install
npm run build              # dist/accso-ai-context.js + dist/ai-context-worker.mjs
./scripts/install-plugin.sh

nodes.title: or, on a fresh machine: mise install && mise run setup

```

Then restart opencode (all running instances).

children.title: What the installer does
children.summary: The installer sets up the OpenCode AI context by installing dependencies and verifying them. It creates a plugin bundle, a shared embedding worker, and a package.json file. The installer runs `bun install` and checks each package, including grammar `.wasm` files. It exits with a non-zero status if any dependencies are missing or incorrect. The `SKIP_DEPS_INSTALL` environment variable can be set to skip dependency installation, and re-running is safe as only the plugin's own entries are modified.
children.bodyText:
## What the installer does

| Target | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `~/.config/opencode/plugins/accso-ai-context.js` | the plugin bundle |
| `~/.config/opencode/ai-context-worker.mjs` | shared embedding worker (kept outside `plugins/` on purpose: opencode loads every file there as a plugin) |
| `~/.config/opencode/package.json` | merged native dependencies (`onnxruntime-node`, `tokenizers`, tree-sitter grammars, ...) |

It runs `bun install` there (npm as fallback) and verifies every package,
including each grammar's `.wasm`; it exits non-zero otherwise. Set
`SKIP_DEPS_INSTALL=1` to leave dependency installation to opencode's next
start. Re-running is safe: only this plugin's own entries are touched.

children.title: First start
children.summary: The documentation covers the setup and initial indexing process for a search index. Key terms include embedding model, shared Hugging Face cache, ai-context.config.yaml, opencode plugin, enabled setting, gitignore, index-status and cross-repo skills, and the creation of the .opencode folder.
children.bodyText:
## First start

- The embedding model (~137 MB, quantized ONNX) is downloaded once into the
  shared Hugging Face cache ([ADR-0005](adr/0005-shared-huggingface-model-cache-directory.md)).
- `.opencode/ai-context.config.yaml` is created if missing (every setting with
  its default, `enabled: false`, never overwritten). **The plugin does nothing
  in a repository until you set `enabled: true` there** (or start opencode with
  `AI_CONTEXT_PLUGIN_ENABLED=1`). Once enabled, it also creates `.opencode/.gitignore` (volatile status file) and the
  `index-status` and `cross-repo` skills under `.opencode/skills/`. The `.opencode` folder is
  created if it does not exist.
- The first index of a repo can take minutes; follow it in
  `.opencode/ai-context/index-status.json` or via `index_status`.

## Updating

Rebuild, re-run `install-plugin.sh`, restart opencode. The shared worker is
replaced automatically once the old one exits (idle 10 min) or you stop it.

description: This plugin exposes telemetry through OpenTelemetry spans and an in-memory summary, and provides status information for JetBrains AI Assistant via ACP. It uses native OS notifications for user-visible status messages and logs for other purposes.

nodes.title: Observability
nodes.summary: This plugin exposes telemetry through two channels and solves problems related to getting status information for users when running under non-OpenCode TUIs, such as JetBrains AI Assistant via ACP.
nodes.bodyText:
# Observability

This plugin exposes telemetry through two complementary channels, and
separately has to solve a harder problem: getting **any** status
information in front of a user at all when the plugin runs under a
frontend that isn't OpenCode's own TUI -- notably **JetBrains AI
Assistant via ACP** (Agent Client Protocol), one of this plugin's
actual deployment targets. Those are two different problems addressed
in the two sections below.

children.title: 1. Tool-call telemetry (OpenTelemetry + in-memory summary)
children.summary: This plugin uses OpenTelemetry to track tool calls in a session, logging both an in-memory summary and OTel spans. It does not bundle an SDK or exporter, allowing existing OpenTelemetry configurations to be used.
children.bodyText:
## 1. Tool-call telemetry (OpenTelemetry + in-memory summary)

See [ADR-0011](adr/0011-otel-bring-your-own-backend-telemetry.md) for
the full decision record. Summary:

- `tool.execute.before`/`tool.execute.after` plugin hooks
  (`src/telemetry/telemetry.ts`) observe **every** tool call in a
  session -- native `grep`/`glob`/`lsp` included, not just this
  plugin's own tools.
- Every observed call is dual-written to:
  - an **in-memory summary**, exposed via the `ai_context_telemetry_report` native
    tool as JSON (per-tool call count, total/average duration,
    approximate input/output token counts) -- zero configuration
    required;
  - a standard **OpenTelemetry span** (`tool.execute:<toolName>`) and a
    **duration histogram** (`opencode.tool.duration`, ms), via
    `@opentelemetry/api`'s global tracer/meter.
- The OTel path is **API-only** -- this plugin does not bundle an SDK
  or exporter. Per the OTel API's own design, calling a tracer/meter
  with no SDK registered is a safe no-op. If the OpenCode host process
  (or the user's environment more broadly) already has an OTel SDK +
  exporter configured, this plugin's spans/metrics show up there
  automatically, with zero plugin-side configuration. If not, the calls
  cost effectively nothing and produce no output.

children.title: How to actually see the OTel data
children.summary: This plugin does not provide a collector or dashboard. To see spans/metrics, register an SDK + exporter in the SAME process OpenCode itself runs in.
children.bodyText:
### How to actually see the OTel data

This plugin does not provide a collector or dashboard. To see spans/
metrics, register an SDK + exporter in the SAME process OpenCode itself
runs in (typically via `NODE_OPTIONS`/an OpenCode startup hook that
loads `@opentelemetry/sdk-node`, or whatever mechanism the OpenCode
host process already supports for its own instrumentation) pointed at
any OTLP-compatible backend (Jaeger, an OTel Collector, etc.). This
plugin's `trace.getTracer("opencode-ai-context-plugin")`/
`metrics.getMeter("opencode-ai-context-plugin")` calls will then be
picked up by that SDK like any other instrumented library in the
process.

children.title: Instrumentation name and signals
children.summary: This documentation covers the instrumentation of a search index, including signals such as `tool.execute:<toolName>`, `opencode.tool.duration`, and `ai_context_telemetry_report`. The `tool.execute:<toolName>` signal includes attributes like `tool`, `sessionID`, and `callID`. The `opencode.tool.duration` signal is a histogram with units in milliseconds, and it includes attributes `tool` and `sessionID`. The `ai_context_telemetry_report` tool output provides per-tool metrics like `callCount`, `totalDurationMs`, `avgDurationMs`, and token counts, which are stored in memory and reset upon process restart.
children.bodyText:
### Instrumentation name and signals

| Signal | Name | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Span | `tool.execute:<toolName>` | Attributes: `tool`, `sessionID`, `callID` |
| Histogram | `opencode.tool.duration` | Unit `ms`; attributes `tool`, `sessionID` |
| `ai_context_telemetry_report` tool output | per-tool `callCount`, `totalDurationMs`, `avgDurationMs`, `totalInputTokens`, `totalOutputTokens`, `totalTokens` | In-memory only, resets when the process restarts |

children.title: 2. Getting plugin status in front of a user across frontends (TUI vs. ACP)
children.summary: This documentation covers how to get plugin status across different frontends (TUI and ACP-based clients like Zed and JetBrains AI Assistant) for opencode plugins. It explains that status mechanisms that work in one frontend do not work in the other, and provides details on how to implement status mechanisms for JetBrains AI Assistant's ACP bridge.
children.bodyText:
## 2. Getting plugin status in front of a user across frontends (TUI vs. ACP)

opencode plugins run under multiple frontends: opencode's own TUI, and
**ACP-based clients** (Zed, **JetBrains AI Assistant** -- one of this
plugin's real deployment targets) that talk to opencode over the Agent
Client Protocol. Status mechanisms that work in one do **not** work in
the other, and this matters directly for this plugin: if it ever needs
to surface a user-visible status ("model download in progress," "index
backup restored," a warning about a malformed backup file, etc.), the
mechanism has to work under JetBrains AI Assistant's ACP bridge, not
just opencode's own TUI.

The full investigation, with source-level citations against opencode's
actual code (not just its type definitions/docs), lives in
[`opencode-plugin-workarounds.md`](opencode-plugin-workarounds.md) --
this section is the short version; read that file for the "why" and
the copy-pasteable implementation.

children.title: Quick reference: what actually reaches the user, by frontend
children.summary: The documentation covers the frontend mechanisms for reaching users, including `client.app.log(...)`, which always lands in the log file, and native OS notifications (`osascript`/`notify-send`). It also mentions that the `"permission.ask"` hook is likely unwired and that `client.tui.showToast(...)` works, but the ACP event bridge has no `tui.toast.show` case.
children.bodyText:
### Quick reference: what actually reaches the user, by frontend

| Mechanism | opencode TUI | ACP (JetBrains AI Assistant, Zed) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `client.tui.showToast(...)` | ✅ Works | ❌ Confirmed dead end -- opencode's ACP event bridge has no `tui.toast.show` case |
| `client.app.log(...)` | ✅ Always lands in the log file | ✅ Always lands in the log file | 
| Injected chat message (`session.prompt` with `noReply: true`) | N/A | ❌ Confirmed dead end -- built as a `user`-role message; the ACP bridge only forwards `assistant`-role parts |
| `"permission.ask"` hook | Likely unwired even in the TUI -- see the workarounds doc | Likely unwired -- no `plugin.trigger(...)` call site found in opencode's permission path |
| **Native OS notification** (`osascript` / `notify-send`, spawned directly) | ✅ Works | ✅ **Works** -- entirely bypasses opencode's hook/event system, so it's frontend-agnostic by construction |

**Practical takeaway for this plugin**: `client.app.log(...)` is fine as
a cheap, always-available secondary channel (nobody's watching it by
default, but it's there for debugging). For anything a user actually
needs to notice under JetBrains AI Assistant/ACP, use a native OS
notification -- see the workarounds doc's §1e for the ready-to-use
`notifyOs()` implementation, including the injectable-runner pattern
needed to keep unit tests from spawning real `osascript`/`notify-send`
processes (§3 of that doc).

children.title: Known opencode-side quirk: double bootstrap
children.summary: The documentation covers the known opencode-side quirk of double plugin bootstrap, which occurs per session and is not fixable by plugins. It also mentions the need for a time-windowed dedup gate for any one-shot, user-visible side effects to prevent users from seeing them fire twice for a session start.
children.bodyText:
### Known opencode-side quirk: double bootstrap

opencode invokes plugin bootstrap **twice** per session (confirmed via
opencode's own logs showing the same `run=<id>` with two independent,
near-simultaneous bootstrap cycles) -- this is opencode-side, not
something a plugin can fix. Any one-shot, user-visible side effect
(e.g. a "plugin loaded" OS notification) needs a time-windowed dedup
gate in front of it, or the user sees it fire twice for what feels like
one session start. See the workarounds doc §2 for the `OsNotifyGate`
pattern (`createOsNotifyGate`) this plugin should use if/when it adds
any bootstrap-time user-visible notification.

children.title: Current status in this plugin
children.summary: The plugin emits OS notifications for indexing events and logs indexing progress through a status file and tool responses. It also logs errors and notices for failed files and provides a mechanism to retry them.
children.bodyText:
### Current status in this plugin

The plugin emits native OS notifications (plugin started; large indexing
run started/finished; indexing failed; `os_notifications: false` or
`AI_CONTEXT_OS_NOTIFICATIONS=0` silences them) but no chat-visible status
messages. Indexing progress (see
[ADR-0018](adr/0018-indexing-progress-via-status-file-and-tool-responses.md))
reaches the user through channels that work under ACP. `total` counts only files that need work; `reasons` says why (`new`, `changed`, `removed`, `upgrade`, `repair`, `summaries`; a forced `reindex_chunks`/`reindex_summaries` run counts as `upgrade`). Self-healing runs (`upgrade`/`repair`/`summaries`) always get an "Updating index" popup naming the reason, see [ADR-0027](adr/0027-self-healing-reindex.md):

Further files sit next to the status file (both git-ignored, written only when the plugin is enabled):

- **`index-tree.md`**: tree of every indexed file with language and chunk count, plus export date, repository, git branch/commit and last index update, and the files that failed. Written by `ai_context_export_index_tree` and after each completed indexing run.
- **`tool.log.md`** (opt-in, `tool_log: true`): one entry per tool call with time, tool, session/call id and arguments, followed by a `↳` entry with the duration and a response summary (size, result counts, first paths, error text, "empty result"). `tool_log_full_responses: true` logs complete arguments and the complete response text, without any truncation. At 5 MB the file is rotated to `tool.<time>.log.md` (newest 10 kept). Use it to see why an agent chose or misused a tool.
- **`error.log.md`**: persistent log of everything that went wrong (every problem that also becomes an OS popup, each failed file with its error, a failed run). Newest entries last, capped at 256 KB (oldest dropped). Unlike popups it is not deduplicated, so it shows how often something fails.

1. **Status file** `.opencode/ai-context/index-status.json`, rewritten at
   most every 2 s (immediately on phase changes and new failures):

   ```json
   {
     "version": 1,
     "running": true,
     "phase": "indexing",
     "done": 412,
     "total": 1900,
     "percent": 21,
     "reasons": { "new": 12, "upgrade": 400 },
     "failed": 1,
     "failures": [
       { "file": "src/big.ts", "error": "EACCES", "attempts": 1, "lastFailedAt": "2026-10-05T08:10:02.000Z" }
     ],
     "currentFile": "src/app/foo.ts",
     "filesPerSec": 6.2,
     "etaSeconds": 240,
     "startedAt": "2026-10-05T08:05:00.000Z",
     "updatedAt": "2026-10-05T08:10:02.000Z",
     "finishedAt": null,
     "lastError": null,
     "notices": []
   }
   ```

   Phases: `idle`, `scanning`, `loading-model` (first-time model
   download), `indexing`, `done`, `failed`. Follow it with
   `while true; do clear; cat .opencode/ai-context/index-status.json; sleep 1; done`. Add the file to
   the project's `.gitignore` (the backup next to it is meant to be
   committed, this file is not).
2. **`index_status`** returns the same data in its `indexing`
   block, including `statusFile`.
3. **`indexingNotice`** in `semantic_search`, `search_docs`
   and `analyze_impact` results while a run is active (arrays are
   wrapped as `{ indexingNotice, results }` only then).

Files that fail to index are skipped and listed under `failures`; a later
change event (file watcher) retries them, success removes the entry,
another failure increments `attempts`.

For anything else that must reach a user outside a tool response (e.g. a
startup warning), follow the table above and update this section with
the mechanism that was actually wired in.

description: This document outlines workarounds for common issues in opencode plugins, including showing plugin status in chat, handling plugin bootstrapping, and managing notifications. It covers various methods for displaying messages and notifications across different frontend environments and provides guidance on avoiding duplicate plugin bootstrapping.

nodes.title: opencode Plugin Workarounds — Reusable Patterns
nodes.summary: This document provides a list of workarounds for opencode's plugin API, ensuring future projects don't have to re-invent them. It includes generic code snippets that can be copied and pasted into opencode plugin projects, without needing to reference the source project's file structure.
nodes.bodyText:
# opencode Plugin Workarounds — Reusable Patterns

This is a standalone, copy-pasteable catalogue of everything this project had to work around
in opencode's plugin API, so future plugin projects don't have to re-derive it from scratch.
Every claim below was verified against opencode's actual source (`sst/opencode`, `dev`
branch) during this project — not inferred from docs alone. Where a claim is "confirmed
dead end," it means we traced the real code path and found no route through, so don't spend
time re-investigating it.

This doc is self-contained: every code snippet below is generic and copy-pasteable as-is
into any opencode plugin project — no reference to this source project's file structure is
required to use it. (It originated in `@accso/opencode-ard-plugin`'s `docs/architecture.md`
§10 and `docs/design-decisions.md`, if you want the fuller "why" narrative behind these
findings — but you don't need those files to use anything here.)

children.title: 0. Plugin entry format: export ONE default `{ id, server }` object
children.summary: The documentation describes how opencode loads plugin modules, including v1 and legacy formats. It outlines the expected structure of a plugin entry file and provides guidance on best practices for exporting functions and ensuring proper functionality.
children.bodyText:
## 0. Plugin entry format: export ONE default `{ id, server }` object

How opencode loads a plugin module (verified against opencode `v1.19.0`,
`packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts` `applyPlugin` / `getLegacyPlugins` and
`plugin/shared.ts` `readV1Plugin`):

1. If `module.default` is an object with `id` / `server`, it is a **v1 plugin**: only
   `default.server(input, options)` is called. This is the current format (SDK type
   `PluginModule` in `@opencode-ai/plugin`). Path/file plugins **must** have an `id`
   (`Path plugin ... must export id`); npm plugins fall back to the package `name`.
2. Otherwise the **legacy loader** runs: it iterates `Object.values(module)` and calls
   **every distinct exported function** as a plugin (de-duplicated by identity only;
   non-function exports throw `Plugin export is not a function`).

Consequences and rules:

```ts
// index.ts -- recommended (v1 format)
import type { PluginModule } from "@opencode-ai/plugin";
import { MyPlugin } from "./plugin.js";

const plugin: PluginModule = { id: "my-plugin", server: MyPlugin };
export default plugin; // the ONLY export
```

- **Never export helper/factory functions from the plugin entry file** (e.g. a testable
  `createHooks(deps)`) next to the plugin. In legacy mode each one is invoked with
  `PluginInput` and silently starts a *second full plugin instance* (duplicate hooks,
  tools, workers, notifications). Import such helpers from their own module in tests.
- `export default fn` plus `export { fn }` is harmless (same reference, de-duplicated);
  `export default fn` plus `export { otherFn }` is not.
- Guard it with a test: `assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(await import("./index")), ["default"])`
  and check `typeof default.id === "string"` / `typeof default.server === "function"`.
- Keep `@opencode-ai/plugin` aligned with the running opencode (`opencode` logs its version
  as `version=` in `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`); diff the SDK `dist/*.d.ts`
  between versions when upgrading. Pin the copy in `~/.config/opencode/package.json` too.

children.title: 1. Problem: there is no reliable, cross-frontend way to show plugin status in chat
children.summary: The documentation covers the challenge of displaying plugin status across different frontend clients, such as opencode's TUI and ACP-based clients. It mentions that status mechanisms that work in one client do not work in the other due to differences in the Agent Client Protocol.
children.bodyText:
## 1. Problem: there is no reliable, cross-frontend way to show plugin status in chat

opencode plugins can run under multiple frontends: opencode's own TUI, and ACP-based clients
(Zed, JetBrains AI Assistant) that talk to opencode over the Agent Client Protocol. Status
mechanisms that work in one do **not** work in the other.

children.title: 1a. `client.tui.showToast(...)` — TUI only, confirmed dead in ACP
children.summary: `client.tui.showToast(...)` is a TUI-only function that displays success messages. It works in opencode's own TUI but is not used by ACP clients, as there is no corresponding event in the ACP event bridge.
children.bodyText:
### 1a. `client.tui.showToast(...)` — TUI only, confirmed dead in ACP

```ts
await client.tui.showToast({
  body: { message: "ARD plugin loaded — 3 skill(s), semantic matching ready.", variant: "success" },
});
```

This works great in opencode's own TUI. **It never reaches ACP clients.** Confirmed by
reading opencode's ACP event bridge (`packages/opencode/src/acp/event.ts`): its event switch
only forwards four event types —`session.status`, `permission.asked`,
`message.part.updated`, `message.part.delta`. There is no `tui.toast.show` case. If your
plugin's only status signal is a toast, ACP users will never see it.

children.title: 1b. `client.app.log(...)` — always works, but requires deliberately looking
children.summary:
- **Function**: `client.app.log` logs messages to the opencode log file.
- **Usage**: Pass a JSON object with `service`, `level`, and `message` keys.
- **Output**: Logs messages to `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`.
- **Notes**: Not user-visible without manual log tailing, suitable for debugging.

children.title: 1c. Injecting a chat-visible assistant message — confirmed dead end
children.summary: The documentation covers injecting a chat-visible assistant message, but it is confirmed to be a dead end. The SDK does not support creating an assistant-authored message directly via the prompt API, as it uses `role: "user"` and the ACP bridge's handlers only accept messages with `metadata.role === "assistant"`.
children.bodyText:
### 1c. Injecting a chat-visible assistant message — confirmed dead end

It's tempting to try creating a message directly via the SDK:

```ts
// DOES NOT WORK for ACP visibility — documented here so you don't retry it.
await client.session.prompt({
  path: { id: sessionId },
  body: { noReply: true, parts: [{ type: "text", text: "Plugin loaded." }] },
});
```

`noReply: true` is real and does create+persist a message without invoking the LLM (confirmed
in `session/prompt.ts`: `if (input.noReply === true) return message`). **But** the message is
built with `role: "user"` (`createUserMessage`), and the ACP bridge's `handlePartDelta`
explicitly early-returns unless `metadata.role === "assistant"`; `handlePartUpdated` ignores
non-tool parts entirely. There is no supported way from a plugin to synthesize an
assistant-authored, ACP-visible chat message. Don't spend time trying variations of this —
we tried role overrides and direct part injection; none reach the ACP chat view.

children.title: 1d. `"permission.ask"` plugin hook — likely never invoked at all
children.summary: The `"permission.ask"` hook is not invoked in the opencode version tested, and its functionality is limited to filtering skills based on their permission evaluation.
children.bodyText:
### 1d. `"permission.ask"` plugin hook — likely never invoked at all

The `Hooks` type (`@opencode-ai/plugin`) documents a `"permission.ask"` hook. We traced the
real permission path exhaustively: `ctx.ask()` (`session/tools.ts`) calls
`Permission.Service.ask()` (`permission/index.ts`) directly — we read that function in full
and found **zero** `plugin.trigger(...)` calls anywhere in it, nor in any other call site we
could find (`session/llm.ts`, `session/processor.ts`, `skill/index.ts`, `plugin/index.ts`,
the HTTP permission route). If your plugin's design depends on an interactive
`"permission.ask"` hook actually firing, verify this against your opencode version first —
in the version we tested against, it's dead code from a plugin author's perspective.
(Traced originally against an older opencode; not re-verified against 1.19.0 -- re-check
before relying on either behaviour.)

The mechanism that **does** actually enforce anything is
`Permission.evaluate("skill", skill.name, agent.permission).action !== "deny"` in
`skill/index.ts` — this filters which skills are even offered to the model at all. If you
need enforcement, hook into whatever your plugin controls that feeds this evaluation (in our
case, we drive the effective permission set for the turn), not an "ask" prompt.

children.title: 1e. The only thing confirmed to work everywhere: native OS notifications
children.summary: The documentation covers the implementation of native OS notifications in the plugin process, which bypasses opencode's hook/event system and works across different platforms. Key terms include `OsNotifyRunner`, `appleScriptString`, `notifyOs`, and platform-specific commands like `osascript` and `notify-send`. The implementation notes mention the need to inject a runner and platform, handle platform-specific quirks like AppleScript's lack of an icon parameter, and provide a configurable option to silence native notifications.

children.title: 2. Problem: plugin bootstrap runs twice per session
children.summary: The documentation covers the issue of a plugin running twice per session, which is observable as a single new session. The key terms include "plugin bootstrap runs twice per session," "symptom," "duplicate-export cause," and "time-windowed dedup gate." The decision is to fix the duplicate-export cause by exporting only `default { id, server }` and to use a time-windowed dedup gate as a workaround for the cache-stampede race.

children.title: 3. Testing gotcha: side-effecting status calls need injectable no-ops in tests
children.summary: This documentation covers the issue of testing a search index that includes side-effecting status calls, such as spawning `osascript` or `notify-send` processes. The key terms are "testing gotcha," "side-effecting status calls," and "injectable no-ops." The decision is to make the notifier and its gate injectable, passing an inert gate from tests to prevent real processes from being spawned during testing.
children.bodyText:
## 3. Testing gotcha: side-effecting status calls need injectable no-ops in tests

Once you wire a real OS-notification (or any other real subprocess-spawning) call into your
plugin's bootstrap function, **every existing test that exercises that bootstrap function with
default/enabled config will now spawn real `osascript`/`notify-send` processes** as a side
effect of running `bun test` / `npm test`. This is easy to miss because the tests still pass —
they just silently launch extra processes.

Fix: always make the notifier and its gate injectable, and pass an inert gate from tests:

```ts
const noOsNotify: OsNotifyGate = { shouldNotify: () => false };

await bootstrapMyPlugin({
  // ...other test options...
  osNotifyGate: noOsNotify,
});
```

Audit every call site that invokes the bootstrap/init function with a config that has the
notification feature enabled (including default configs!) and inject the inert gate/runner.
This is not optional — treat "spawns real OS processes during `bun test`" as a bug whenever
you add any subprocess-spawning side effect to code under test.

children.title: 4. Enabling opencode's native `lsp` tool from a plugin
children.summary: This documentation explains how to enable the native LSP tool in opencode 1.19.0 using a plugin. It covers setting `config.lsp` to enable built-in servers and the `experimentalLspTool` flag to register the tool. The documentation also notes that setting the environment variable `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_LSP_TOOL` inside a plugin is best-effort and requires exporting the variable in the environment that starts opencode.
children.bodyText:
## 4. Enabling opencode's native `lsp` tool from a plugin

opencode 1.19.0 (`lsp/lsp.ts`, `tool/registry.ts`): LSP servers start only when
`config.lsp` is truthy, and the `lsp` *tool* is registered only when the runtime flag
`experimentalLspTool` (env `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_LSP_TOOL`) is on.

- Setting `config.lsp = {}` from a plugin `config` hook works (any truthy value enables the
  built-in servers; never override an explicit `lsp: false`).
- Setting `process.env.OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_LSP_TOOL` inside the plugin is **best-effort
  only**: flags are read through `RuntimeFlags` when the registry layer is built, which
  can happen before plugins load. Document that users must export the variable in the
  environment that starts opencode.

children.title: Quick reference: what to try, in order, for cross-frontend plugin status
children.summary: This documentation provides a quick reference for cross-frontend plugin status, listing four methods to notify users and their key terms and decisions.
children.bodyText:
## Quick reference: what to try, in order, for cross-frontend plugin status

1. `client.app.log(...)` — cheap, always works, but nobody's watching the log by default.
2. `client.tui.showToast(...)` — nice UX, but silently invisible under ACP. Fine as a
   secondary channel if you also have #3.
3. Native OS notification (`osascript` / `notify-send`) via a directly-spawned subprocess —
   the only mechanism confirmed to work under every frontend, at the cost of being a native
   popup outside the chat UI itself. Make it configurable and default it as you see fit.
4. Don't bother with: ACP toast forwarding, `noReply` message injection for
   assistant-authored chat visibility, or relying on `"permission.ask"` actually firing —
   all confirmed dead ends against opencode's current implementation. Re-verify against your
   opencode version's source before assuming otherwise; don't just trust the type
   definitions/docs, since `"permission.ask"` is a documented type that turned out to be
   unwired in practice.

children.title: Feature matrix
children.summary: This feature matrix outlines the various tools, hooks, and storage components of a search index, detailing their states, notes, and associated ADRs. It covers tools like semantic search, repo structure, impact analysis, document indexing, and more, along with hooks for compaction and system-prompt management. The storage section includes SQLite files per project, backup options, and allowlists. The runtime features include progress tracking, token and memory caps, and a shared embedding worker process. Observability is supported through log files and telemetry APIs.

children.title: Differences to the original `.ai-context` stack
children.summary: This table compares the `.ai-context` stack to a new stack using SQLite files and native OpenAI-compatible tools. It includes differences in database, re-ranking method, server components, LSP bridge features, symbol resolution, and file summaries.
children.bodyText:
## Differences to the original `.ai-context` stack

| Original | Plugin |
| --- | --- |
| Postgres + Qdrant, Docker | SQLite files, no Docker |
| ColBERT re-rank (inference service) | Small cross-encoder re-rank (`reranker`) on FTS5 + vector fusion, no always-on service |
| MCP server + LSP bridge + watcher container | Native opencode tools; opencode's own `lsp` tool |
| `resolve_symbol` (LSP bridge) | `find_symbol` (symbol index) + opencode's native `lsp`; provenance trace and structural roles not ported |
| L1 file summaries (local LLM) | File summaries: deterministic, or written by a local OpenAI-compatible LLM (`summary_llm`, default oMLX); routing LLM not ported; fallback summaries are redone once the LLM answers, `reindex_chunks`/`reindex_summaries` force a re-index ([ADR-0027](adr/0027-self-healing-reindex.md)) |

children.title: Behaviour change: opt-in per repository
children.summary: The plugin is enabled per repository, requiring `enabled: true` in `.opencode/ai-context.config.yaml`.
children.bodyText:
## Behaviour change: opt-in per repository

Since ADR-0029 the plugin is off in every repository whose
`.opencode/ai-context.config.yaml` lacks `enabled: true`. Existing config files
are not migrated; add the key by hand.

children.title: Known limitations
children.summary: This documentation outlines the known limitations of the search index, including performance issues with brute-force search, edge analysis limitations, and the scope of semantic search. It also mentions experimental features and memory management considerations.
children.bodyText:
## Known limitations

- Brute-force search: ~110 ms at 2k chunks, ~580 ms at 10k, ~1.75 s at 30k
  chunks (768 dims, measured during the storage spike). Very large repos will
  need an ANN index or `embed_dims` truncation.
- `analyze_impact` edges are name-based; ambiguous edges are flagged, confirm
  with the native `lsp` tool.
- `semantic_search` covers source code only; Markdown documents are reachable
  through `search_docs`.
- The memory guard is a soft ceiling checked between files; the hard bound is
  `embed_max_tokens`.
- `experimental.chat.system.transform` is experimental in opencode; without it
  only the tool descriptions steer the agent.
- Not yet verified: long-running sessions with many ACP instances; the exact
  per-instance RSS after the startup memory fix.
- `heavy_mode` has no functional effect (kept as plumbing).

children.title: Roadmap
children.summary: Retrieval quality plan: Evaluate adoption after a few days, move indexer to shared worker, add compaction hook and `resolve_symbol`, configure `repo_structure` entry cap, and optionally enable tree-sitter chunking for regex-only languages.
children.bodyText:
## Roadmap

Retrieval quality plan: [ADR-0024](adr/0024-retrieval-quality-roadmap.md).

1. Evaluate adoption (`ai_context_telemetry_report`, `view: "adoption"`) after
   a few days; add a grep nudge only if needed.
2. ADR-0022 phase 1: move the indexer into the shared worker.
3. Compaction hook and `resolve_symbol`.
4. Worker PID in `index_status`; configurable `repo_structure` entry cap.
5. Optional tree-sitter chunking for the regex-only languages.

description: This document provides a comprehensive guide for testing the `.ai-context` search index, covering three tiers of verification: unit tests, integration tests, and end-to-end (E2E) tests. It outlines the setup, commands for running each tier, and the shared fixture corpus used for testing. The document also mentions known gaps and limitations in the test suite.

nodes.title: Testing `.ai-context`
nodes.summary: This document provides a reference for the `.ai-context` search index, covering three tiers and commands for testing. It also mentions that `.ai-monitoring` and `.ai-benchmark` are separate tools and not covered here.
nodes.bodyText:
# Testing `.ai-context`

Three independently-runnable tiers, so an AI coding agent (or a human) can
match verification cost to the blast radius of a change — matching the
"tight verify-and-correct loop" discipline in
`.github/instructions/ai-workflow.instructions.md`. Scope note:
`.ai-monitoring` and `.ai-benchmark` are separate tools moving to their own
repos and are **not** covered here.

**This document is the reference** (tiers, commands, fixture corpus,
environment setup). For the test-driven **workflow** to follow when making
a change — red/green/refactor, which tier to add a test to, how to handle
a discovered bug — see
`.github/instructions/ai-context-tdd.instructions.md`.

> **`opencode-ai-context-plugin/` has its own, simpler test setup.** Since
> the plugin has no Postgres/Qdrant/Docker dependency at all (SQLite,
> in-process), its three-tier *workflow discipline* still applies (see
> `.github/instructions/ai-context-tdd.instructions.md`, which covers both
> projects) but its actual runner is single-tier:
> `opencode-ai-context-plugin/test/unit/*.test.ts`, run via
> `npm run test:unit` (plain `node --test`, no `scripts/test.sh`, no
> Docker, no fixture corpus separate from this one — everything the
> plugin does is fast enough to be "Tier 1" in practice). Don't run this
> doc's `scripts/test.sh` for plugin changes, and don't run
> `npm run test:unit` for changes to this Docker stack — the two test
> suites are entirely independent.

children.title: Quick start
children.summary: This section provides instructions for setting up and running a search index. It covers key terms such as indexing, search engine setup, and configuration options.
children.bodyText:
## Quick start

```bash

nodes.title: One-time setup (see "Environment setup" below for details)
nodes.summary: This command installs the necessary dependencies for running a search index. It includes requirements from multiple files and directories, such as `requirements-test.txt`, `watcher/requirements.txt`, `lsp-bridge/requirements.txt`, and `scripts/requirements.txt`. After installing the dependencies, it changes to the `mcp-server` directory and installs its npm packages.
nodes.bodyText:

pip install -r requirements-test.txt -r watcher/requirements.txt \

nodes.title: Run a tier
nodes.summary: This script runs tests for a search index, covering different tiers and components. Key terms include `unit`, `watcher`, `integration`, `e2e`, and `all`.
nodes.bodyText:
# Run a tier
scripts/test.sh unit                 # Tier 1, every component — seconds, no Docker
scripts/test.sh unit watcher         # Tier 1, just watcher/
scripts/test.sh integration          # Tier 1+2 — adds disposable Postgres/Qdrant
scripts/test.sh e2e                  # Tier 1+2+3 — adds the full pipeline, minutes
scripts/test.sh all                  # every tier
```

children.title: Which tier to run for which change
children.summary: This table outlines which tier to run for different types of changes in the search index. The tiers are `unit`, `integration`, and `e2e`. For changes in logic files like `chunker.py`, `symbol_extractor.py`, etc., use the `unit` tier. For changes in database and backend files like `db.ts`, `indexer.py`, etc., use the `integration` tier. For changes that cross components, use the `e2e` tier. If unsure or touching multiple areas, use the `all` tier. The `analyze_impact` tool is recommended for double-checking blast radius before choosing a tier.
children.bodyText:
## Which tier to run for which change

| You changed... | Run |
|---|---|
| `chunker.py`, `symbol_extractor.py`, `import_extractor.py`, `validate_config.py`, `context_assembler.ts`, `range_slice.ts` (pure logic, no DB/network) | `scripts/test.sh unit` |
| `db.ts`'s `analyzeImpact`, `indexer.py`'s delta-upsert/self-heal, `dependency_restore.py`, `inference/main.py` (backend selection/routing) | `scripts/test.sh integration` |
| Anything crossing components (indexing → MCP tool response), `backup.py`, `lsp-bridge/main.py`'s routing | `scripts/test.sh e2e` |
| Not sure / touched multiple areas | `scripts/test.sh all` |

`analyze_impact` (the real MCP tool, not the test) is a good way to double-check
blast radius before picking a tier — if it shows callers/callees outside the
file you changed, favor the broader tier.

children.title: The three tiers
children.summary: The three tiers of the search index documentation cover different stages of indexing and processing, from pure function operations to full pipeline execution.
children.bodyText:
## The three tiers

| Tier | What | Needs | Speed |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 — Unit** | Pure functions: chunk boundaries, symbol/import extraction, config validation, query expansion, keyword rerank, line-range slicing, ColBERT MaxSim scoring (`inference/maxsim.py`) | Nothing — no Docker, no network | Seconds |
| **2 — Integration** | Logic touching Postgres/Qdrant: `analyze_impact` traversal, indexer delta-upsert/self-heal, dependency-restore command selection, inference service backend selection/routing | Disposable Postgres/Qdrant containers (or mocked subprocess/HTTP) | Tens of seconds |
| **3 — E2E** | Full pipeline: real indexing → real MCP tools over real HTTP+MCP protocol; backup/restore round-trip | Real Docker containers (Postgres, Qdrant) + Python/Node processes | Minutes |

children.title: Layout
children.summary: This directory structure outlines a search index setup, including test configurations, scripts, and fixtures for various components like pytest, watcher, lsp-bridge, inference, mcp-server, and E2E tests.
children.bodyText:
### Layout

```
.ai-context/
  pytest.ini                          Python test config (all components)
  requirements-test.txt               pytest, pytest-asyncio, responses
  watcher/tests/{unit,integration}/
  lsp-bridge/tests/{unit,integration}/
  scripts/tests/unit/
  inference/tests/{unit,integration}/    unit: maxsim.py scoring (pure logic)
                                          integration: main.py routing/backends
  mcp-server/test/{unit,integration,e2e}/
  tests/fixtures/sample-repo/          shared multi-language fixture corpus
  tests/e2e/*.py                       Python helper scripts the TS E2E
                                        tests spawn as subprocesses (real
                                        watcher indexing/backup code, run
                                        out-of-process since this codebase's
                                        watcher is Python and the E2E test
                                        harness lives in TS)
  scripts/test.sh                      tier-selectable runner (this doc's
                                        "Quick start" commands)
  scripts/test-cleanup.sh              idempotent Docker cleanup — see below
```

children.title: The shared fixture corpus
children.summary: The shared fixture corpus includes a Kotlin file, a TypeScript file with a decorator and switch statement, a Vue SFC, a Python file with `match`, a Java/C# pair, and two Markdown docs. It is used to test chunking and indexing behaviors across three tiers of the search index pipeline.
children.bodyText:
## The shared fixture corpus

`tests/fixtures/sample-repo/` (see its own `README.md`) is one small,
deliberately-crafted multi-language repo referenced by **all three tiers** —
a Kotlin file (regex-fallback chunking), a TS file with a decorator +
switch statement (tree-sitter + dispatch-arm sub-chunking), a Vue SFC, a
Python file with `match`, a Java/C# pair, and two Markdown docs (above/below
the tree-index heading threshold). Tier 1 asserts chunk boundaries directly
on these files; Tier 2 asserts DB rows after indexing them; Tier 3 asserts
MCP tool responses after the real pipeline indexes them. This means a Tier
3 failure can usually be root-caused by checking whether the matching Tier
1/2 assertion on the same fixture still passes.

Keep this corpus small and deliberate — add a file only when a new
chunking/indexing behavior needs fixture coverage nothing existing already
provides.

children.title: Environment setup
children.summary:
- **Python**: Install dependencies using `pip` for various packages, including `mise` for Python version management and `tree-sitter-languages` for language parsing.
- **TypeScript**: Install dependencies using `npm` for TypeScript development.
- **Docker**: Required for Tier 2 and Tier 3 to run the full pipeline, but not needed for Tier 1.
children.bodyText:
## Environment setup

- **Python**: `pip install -r requirements-test.txt -r watcher/requirements.txt -r lsp-bridge/requirements.txt -r scripts/requirements.txt -r inference/requirements.txt` (the last one is fully optional now — `inference`'s Tier 1/2 suites monkeypatch model loading entirely, so neither `fastembed` nor `onnxruntime` need to be installed to run them; only needed if you want to actually exercise real model inference locally outside Docker). Requires **Python 3.12** (`mise install python@3.12` — pinned in `mise.toml` to match the Docker images; `tree-sitter-languages` doesn't yet support 3.13+).
- **TypeScript**: `cd mcp-server && npm install`. No extra test framework — `node --test` (built-in) + the already-present `ts-node` devDependency.
- **Docker**: required for Tier 2 (`analyze_impact`, `indexer.py`, `inference` — Postgres/Qdrant) and Tier 3 (adds the full pipeline). Not needed for Tier 1 at all.

children.title: Cleanup — no leftover containers
children.summary: This documentation covers cleanup procedures for Docker resources labeled with `com.ai-context.test=true` or running under names matching `ai_context_test_*`, ensuring they are safe to run concurrently with a real dev stack. It includes scripts for idempotent cleanup (`test-cleanup.sh`) and verification (`--check`), as well as automatic cleanup during test runs.
children.bodyText:
## Cleanup — no leftover containers

Every Tier 2/3 Docker resource carries `--label com.ai-context.test=true`
(or runs under a container name matching `ai_context_test_*`), on ports
distinct from the real dev stack (`5433`/`6333`) — confirmed safe to run
**concurrently** with an already-running real dev stack.

- `scripts/test-cleanup.sh` — idempotent, safe to run any time. Run it if
  a previous test run was interrupted/crashed (an agent's own shell
  session being killed mid-run is a real scenario, not hypothetical).
- `scripts/test-cleanup.sh --check` — lists any lingering test resources
  without removing them (exits non-zero if anything is found) — use this
  to *verify* the machine is clean instead of assuming.
- `scripts/test.sh` already runs cleanup as a pre-flight step before every
  `integration`/`e2e` invocation, and traps `EXIT`/`INT`/`TERM` to run it
  again afterward — this is automatic, you don't need to call
  `test-cleanup.sh` yourself in the normal case.

children.title: Known gaps / accepted limitations (found while writing these tests)
children.summary:
- **Known gaps in Kotlin symbol extraction**: `interface` misclassified as `class`.
- **Test file pattern limitation**: Only recognizes JS/TS conventions, not Python's `test_*.py` or top-level `tests/`.
- **Backup/restore limitations**: Only rebuilds `symbol_index`, `import_edges`, and `call_edges` after a reindex.
- **Real multilspy+jedi-language-server round-trip**: Hangs in sandboxed test environment.
- **DI inconsistency**: `deriveQdrantUrl()` reads `process.env.QDRANT_URL` directly instead of `qdrantUrl` value.
children.bodyText:
## Known gaps / accepted limitations (found while writing these tests)

These are documented as explicit "known gap" tests (not silently patched
over) so they can't regress further unnoticed. Fixing them is a separate,
future change — out of scope for the test suite itself:

- **Kotlin `interface` misclassified as `class`** in `symbol_extractor.py`
  (tree-sitter Kotlin grammar emits `class_declaration` for both) — see
  `watcher/tests/unit/test_symbol_extractor.py`.
- **`TEST_FILE_PATTERN`** (`db.ts`, used by `analyze_impact`'s test-coverage
  detection) only recognizes JS/TS conventions, not Python's `test_*.py` or
  a top-level `tests/` directory — see
  `mcp-server/test/integration/analyze_impact.test.ts`.
- **Backup/restore doesn't cover `symbol_index`/`import_edges`/`call_edges`**
  — only a reindex rebuilds those after a restore — see
  `mcp-server/test/e2e/backup_restore.test.ts`.
- **Real multilspy+jedi-language-server round-trip hangs** in this
  sandboxed test environment at the LSP `initialize` handshake — the
  `resolve_symbol` test suite (`lsp-bridge/tests/integration/test_main_resolve_symbol.py`)
  covers this codebase's own routing/validation logic with the language
  server mocked instead. Real round-trip testing needs a different
  environment (e.g. the actual Docker image) or further debugging.
- **`context_assembler.ts`'s `deriveQdrantUrl()`** reads `process.env.QDRANT_URL`
  directly instead of the `qdrantUrl` value threaded through
  `SharedServices`/`createProjectServer` (unlike `get_file`, which uses the
  injected value correctly) — harmless in production (both are always set
  from the same source at container startup) but a real DI inconsistency,
  found via `mcp-server/test/e2e/test-stack.ts`.

## Naming scheme ([ADR-0023](adr/0023-tool-naming-and-descriptions.md))

- **Research tools**, used by the agent while working, no prefix.
- **Admin tools**, used by the user on request, prefix `ai_context_`.

children.title: Research tools
children.summary: The `Research tools` table provides a comprehensive list of search index tools, each designed for specific use cases. The `repo_structure` tool lists directories and files, while `semantic_search` answers conceptual questions about source code. `analyze_impact` helps determine the impact of changes, `find_symbol` locates definitions, and `search_docs` retrieves documentation. The index status provides information on indexing progress and completeness.
children.bodyText:
## Research tools

| Tool | Use when | Arguments | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `repo_structure` | You are new to a project or area; replaces listing directories one by one | `dir_path?`, `depth?`, `project?` (name of another allowed project, no hash) | Directories first with file count and languages, then files |
| `semantic_search` | Conceptual question about **source code** ("where do we retry failed requests?") | `query`, `limit?` | Ranked chunks: path, line range, symbol, score, `project`; follow up with `read` on the line range |
| `analyze_impact` | Before changing, renaming or removing a function/class/method | `symbolName`, `path?`, `direction?` (callers/callees/both), `depth?`, `project?` (another allowed project) | Callers/callees/importers with file and line, plus `tests` (test files that import or call the symbol); edges are name-based, ambiguous ones flagged, confirm with `lsp` |
| `find_symbol` | You know (part of) a class/function/method name and want its definition | `query`, `kind?`, `limit?`, `project?` (another allowed project) | Matches with path, line range, kind, container, plus `tests` (test files that import or call them); exact references via native `lsp` |
| `search_docs` | Docs, ADRs, RFCs, design decisions (Markdown) | `query` (keywords), `mode?` (`toc_only`, `summary_only`, `node_text`), `limit?`, `project?` (another allowed project) | Matching sections from the document trees |
| `index_status` | Empty or partial results, or an `indexingNotice` in a response | `limit?` | File/chunk counts, newest `indexed_at`, recent changes, live progress, failed files |

`semantic_search` does not cover Markdown documents (they are stored as a tree,
not chunked); use `search_docs` for them. Results are fused from vector search and FTS5 BM25 (reciprocal rank fusion) and
re-ranked by a small cross-encoder (`reranker`). Chunks of type `file-summary`
describe a whole file. Exact identifiers: `find_symbol` or `grep`.

While an index run is active, results carry an `indexingNotice` so the agent
knows they may be incomplete.

children.title: Admin tools
children.summary: Admin tools for managing search index projects, including listing, deleting, exporting backups and trees, allowing new repositories, and reporting telemetry.
children.bodyText:
## Admin tools

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `ai_context_list_projects` | List indexed projects (name, key, size); use the `name` as `project` argument |
| `ai_context_delete_project` | Remove a project's stored index |
| `ai_context_export_backup` | Write the JSONL backup into `.opencode/ai-context/backup/` now |
| `ai_context_export_index_tree` | Write `.opencode/ai-context/index-tree.md`: tree of all indexed files (language, chunks) with export date, repo, branch/commit and last index update; also refreshed after each completed indexing run |
| `ai_context_allow_repo` | Add another indexed project to this repo's cross-search allowlist (name validated against the registry; stored as name without hash under `allowed_repos` in the config YAML, so it can be shared); takes effect immediately, no restart |
| `ai_context_telemetry_report` | Per-tool call counts, duration, approximate tokens; `view: "adoption"` shows context tools vs. grep/glob |

children.title: Data boundary
children.summary: The documentation covers the data boundary for tool results, explaining that they are returned to the agent and then to the model provider, which may not be local.
children.bodyText:
## Data boundary

Tool results (code, document text, summaries) are returned to the agent and from there to its model provider, which may not be local. See [data-boundary.md](data-boundary.md).

children.title: Steering the agent
children.summary: The documentation covers the steering of an agent using three layers: system-prompt hint, tool descriptions, and bundled skills. It includes details on the `agent_hint`, `ai_context_export_backup`, `ai_context_export_index_tree`, and other tools, as well as the `index-status` and `cross-repo` skills. The effect of these features is measured using `ai_context_telemetry_report`.
children.bodyText:
## Steering the agent

Three layers, strongest first ([ADR-0020](adr/0020-steer-agent-to-context-tools.md)):

1. **System-prompt hint** (`agent_hint`): a short rule block appended through
   `experimental.chat.system.transform`. It also maps "create an ai context backup" to `ai_context_export_backup` and "which files are indexed" to `ai_context_export_index_tree`. With `enabled` off (default) no tools and no hint are provided.
2. **Tool descriptions**: what the tool covers and does not, when to use it (in the words a user would say, e.g. "create an ai context backup"), what it returns, the next step. Destructive tools (`ai_context_delete_project`) tell the agent to confirm with the user first.
3. **Bundled skills**, on demand only: `index-status` (progress and tuning) and `cross-repo` (look into other indexed projects: `ai_context_list_projects` → `ai_context_allow_repo` → `project` argument).

Measure the effect with `ai_context_telemetry_report` (`view: "adoption"`).

description: This documentation covers troubleshooting issues related to the OpenCode AI Context plugin, including enabling the plugin, checking indexing status, managing summaries, handling stuck indexing processes, memory issues, and tool results. It also discusses shared worker problems, renaming tools, resetting projects, and managing cross-repo access.

nodes.title: Troubleshooting
nodes.summary: Troubleshooting guide for search index issues. Key terms include: troubleshooting, search index, issues, solutions.
nodes.bodyText: # Troubleshooting

children.title: The plugin does nothing / no tools in a repository
children.summary: The plugin is opt-in per repository and requires `enabled` to be set to `true` in `.opencode/ai-context.config.yaml`.
children.bodyText:
## The plugin does nothing / no tools in a repository

The plugin is opt-in per repository (ADR-0029). Check
`.opencode/ai-context.config.yaml`: `enabled` must be `true` (a missing key or a
malformed file counts as off), then restart opencode. `AI_CONTEXT_PLUGIN_ENABLED`
overrides the file in both directions.

children.title: Indexing seems stuck, fan is loud
children.summary: The documentation covers indexing issues, including stuck processes and loud fan noises. It provides guidance on checking the status with `index_status`, adjusting settings like `embed_threads`, `exclude`, and `embed_max_tokens`, and offers a live view with the bundled `watch-index-status.sh` skill.
children.bodyText:
## Indexing seems stuck, fan is loud

Read `.opencode/ai-context/index-status.json` or call `index_status`.
`phase`: `idle | scanning | loading-model | indexing | done | failed`.
`loading-model` is the one-time model load. Lower `embed_threads`, exclude
generated code with `exclude:`, lower `embed_max_tokens` / `max_file_bytes`.
Live view: the bundled `index-status` skill ships `watch-index-status.sh`.

children.title: Summaries are plain text and a popup says "API key not set"
children.summary: The text covers the error "API key not set" and provides instructions to export the API key, restart OpenCode, and enable reindexing summaries.
children.bodyText:
## Summaries are plain text and a popup says "API key not set"

The summary LLM answered HTTP 401. Export the key and restart opencode:
`export AI_CONTEXT_SUMMARY_LLM_API_KEY=<your key>` (or the variable named by
`api_key_env`). Then set `reindex_summaries: true` to rewrite the fallback
summaries now (they are also redone automatically on the next start). The same
hint is in `notices` of `index_status`.

children.title: A second session starts indexing again
children.summary: This documentation describes how search indexing works in a system, including the process of starting a new session, handling existing locks, and managing leftover locks from crashed processes. Key terms include `index.lock`, ADR-0025, and plugin versions.
children.bodyText:
## A second session starts indexing again

Since ADR-0025 only one process indexes a project (`index.lock` in the project
data directory); other sessions wait and skip files that are already indexed.
Sessions running an older plugin version ignore the lock: restart them.
A leftover lock of a crashed process is taken over after at most 45 s.

children.title: Indexing failed with a memory message
children.summary: The search index failed due to memory constraints. To resolve, adjust `embed_max_tokens`, `max_file_bytes`, or increase `max_memory_mb`. Refer to ADR-0019 for guidance.
children.bodyText:
## Indexing failed with a memory message

The `max_memory_mb` guard stopped the run. Lower `embed_max_tokens` and
`max_file_bytes`, or raise `max_memory_mb`. See
[ADR-0019](adr/0019-bounded-memory-during-indexing.md).

children.title: `ACP process exited unexpectedly. Exit code: 137` / `database is locked` in `Cache.db`
children.summary: This error indicates that the `ACP process` exited unexpectedly with an exit code of 137, which is a common sign of out-of-memory conditions. The SQLite database in `Cache.db` is locked, suggesting that the host's macOS HTTP cache is under memory pressure. To resolve this issue, check for stale `opencode acp` processes with high RSS and end them by PID.
children.bodyText:
## `ACP process exited unexpectedly. Exit code: 137` / `database is locked` in `Cache.db`

Exit 137 is an out-of-memory kill. The SQLite lock messages come from the
macOS HTTP cache of the host and are a symptom of memory pressure, not of this
plugin's stores. Look for stale `opencode acp` processes with high RSS
(`ps -axo pid,rss,command | grep opencode`) and end old ones by PID.
Expected: one `opencode acp` per session plus one embedding worker.

children.title: Tool results are empty or partial
children.summary: The search index is currently running, and results may be empty or partial. Check `index_status` for updates. For Markdown documents, use `search_docs` instead of `semantic_search`.
children.bodyText:
## Tool results are empty or partial

Indexing may still be running (`indexingNotice` in the response). Check
`index_status`. For Markdown documents use `search_docs`, not `semantic_search`.

children.title: Agent still prefers grep
children.summary: The documentation covers the use of `grep` as a search index and mentions that the system hook is experimental in opencode.
children.bodyText:
## Agent still prefers grep

Check `agent_hint` is not disabled and look at the adoption view:
`ai_context_telemetry_report` with `view: "adoption"`. The system hook is
experimental in opencode; without it only tool descriptions apply.

children.title: Shared worker problems
children.summary: This documentation covers issues related to shared workers in a search index. It explains the log file location (`<data_dir>/embed-worker.log`), the socket path (`<data_dir>/embed-worker.sock`), and how to disable shared workers with environment variables or configuration settings. If shared workers are disabled, the plugin falls back to in-process embedding and replaces a stale socket on the next start.
children.bodyText:
## Shared worker problems

Log: `<data_dir>/embed-worker.log`. Socket: `<data_dir>/embed-worker.sock`.
Disable with `shared_worker: false` or `AI_CONTEXT_SHARED_WORKER=0`; the
plugin falls back to in-process embedding. A stale socket is replaced on the
next start.

children.title: Old tool names
children.summary: This documentation covers the renaming of three old tool names: `ai_context_search_docs`, `ai_context_index_status`, and `telemetry_report`. The changes were made according to ADR-0023 without creating aliases. The prompt and skills need to be updated to reflect these changes.
children.bodyText:
## Old tool names

`ai_context_search_docs`, `ai_context_index_status` and `telemetry_report`
were renamed (ADR-0023) without aliases; update prompts and skills.

children.title: Reset a project
children.summary: The `ai_context_delete_project` function removes the stored index and rebuilds it on the next start or restores from a backup.
children.bodyText:
## Reset a project

`ai_context_delete_project` removes the stored index; it is rebuilt on the next
start (or restored from `.opencode/ai-context/backup/`).

children.title: `Unknown or not allowed project`
children.summary: This tool checks if a specified project is allowed in the current repository. If not, it uses the `cross-repo` skill to list all projects and then allows the specified project. If the project is not found, it indicates that the repository was never indexed with this plugin.
children.bodyText:
## `Unknown or not allowed project`

A tool was called with `project: "<name>"` for a repo that is not on this
repo's allowlist. Use the `cross-repo` skill: `ai_context_list_projects` for the
exact `name` (no hash; a hashed key is not accepted), then
`ai_context_allow_repo`. It applies immediately. If the name is
missing from the list, that repo was never indexed with this plugin.
